---
title: "A second on.exit() erases the first"
ref: FUN-10
categories: [Functions]
impact: silencieux
attendu: "both cleanup actions run"
versions: "All"
source: "General R knowledge"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
process <- function() {
  on.exit(cat("close the connection\n"))
  on.exit(cat("delete the temporary file\n"))
  invisible(NULL)
}
process()
```
:::

## Why

`on.exit()` records code to run when the function exits. By default, each call replaces whatever was recorded before. Here, closing the connection is forgotten without any message.

The pitfall often hides in a long function, where the second `on.exit()` is added dozens of lines after the first.

## The fix

Add `add = TRUE` to every call. The actions then run in the order they were declared, or in reverse order with `after = FALSE`.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
process <- function() {
  on.exit(cat("close the connection\n"), add = TRUE)
  on.exit(cat("delete the temporary file\n"), add = TRUE)
  invisible(NULL)
}
process()
```
:::
